scope: Parent independently reproduced the Engram preflight diagnosis on private copies. No real store was opened, written, repaired or migrated; read-only cp -a plus a directory listing.

commands.stderr: compatibility: unsafe or invalid fixture metadata

conclusion: The rejection is the preflight's own rule at internal/store/compatibility.go L60 (any -wal/-shm/-journal entry), not store damage. The identical instance_id in the successful probe is the real store's identity, so the copy was faithful.
counter_evidence_preserved: The same error also appears on a freshly created temporary store with sidecars, and a live writer changing directory metadata can trigger it without sidecars; the message never names the failing condition.
real_store_effect: engram.db, engram.db-wal, engram.db-shm, .instance-id and locks kept identical sizes and mtimes. sync.log kept growing because the pre-existing engram serve process writes it, not this check.
limits: cp -a taken while engram serve held the store open, so it is not an atomic snapshot and proves nothing about original-store integrity. No memory contents were dumped. This is a preflight-diagnosis verification, not an Engram integration test.
